scenes.tts: This protein sits in the right place, at the right time. Does that tell you what it does? Here are two possible answers, each true in its own cell.
scenes.caption: This protein sits in the right place, at the right time. Does that tell you what it does? Here are two possible answers, each true in its own cell.
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film. Two identical round cells in cross-section, side by side, each filling about 65% of frame height: left outlined TEAL, right outlined ORANGE. Inside each, a small purple blob labelled 'protein X' drifts slowly along the same path in both, so the twins move in step. On 'two possible answers', a label settles over each cell: left 'Model 1', right 'Model 2'. A wide empty bar appears across the bottom. The question appears across the top in white: 'Does the right place tell you the job?'
scenes.narration: This protein sits in the right place, at the right time. Does that tell you what it does? Here are two possible answers, each true in its own cell.

scenes.visual: Title 'Where the Twins Disagree' fades in over the top of the two cells for 2 seconds while the purple blobs keep drifting. The hook's question text fades out beneath it.

scenes.tts: Call the cells twins: identical, except each has a different model built in. Every experiment runs on both at once. Here is the rule: a result can choose only where the twins disagree.
scenes.caption: Call the cells twins: identical, except each has a different model built in. Every experiment runs on both at once. Here is the rule: a result can choose only where the twins disagree.
scenes.visual: On 'twins', a thin white bracket joins the two cells at the top. On 'runs on both at once', a single pipette descends from above, splits in two and touches both cells together; both flash a soft white rim at the same moment. On 'the rule', the bottom bar lights up and demonstrates its two states: grey 'SAME' on its left half, GOLD 'DIFFERENT' on its right half, with a pointer sliding once across and back to rest between them.
scenes.narration: Call the cells twins: identical, except each has a different model built in. Every experiment runs on both at once. Here is the rule: a result can choose only where the twins disagree.

scenes.tts: First question: where does the protein live? Model one, in the teal twin: in lysosomes. Model two, in the orange twin: in mitochondria. Break both cells open and spin the pieces, at rising speeds, into five tubes.
scenes.caption: First question: where does the protein live? Model one, in the teal twin: in lysosomes. Model two, in the orange twin: in mitochondria. Break both cells open and spin the pieces, at rising speeds, into five tubes.
scenes.visual: The purple blob in the teal cell settles inside a small round compartment; in the orange cell, inside a longer rounded one. Show them first, then label them 'lysosome' and 'mitochondrion' a beat later. On 'break both cells open', each cell loses its outline and its contents tip into a row of five tall tubes drawn beneath it, labelled N, M, L, P, S, filling smoothly from the left, with a small arrow under the row reading 'rising spin speed'. Both rows build at the same time and stay on screen; the cells shrink to small teal and orange badges at the top.
scenes.narration: First question: where does the protein live? Model one, in the teal twin: in lysosomes. Model two, in the orange twin: in mitochondria. Break both cells open and spin the pieces, at rising speeds, into five tubes.

scenes.tts: Test one. Is the protein enriched in tube L, more concentrated than in the starting mix? In the teal twin, yes. In the orange twin, also yes: tube L holds plenty of mitochondria. This test cannot choose.
scenes.caption: Test one. Is the protein enriched in tube L, more concentrated than in the starting mix? In the teal twin, yes. In the orange twin, also yes: tube L holds plenty of mitochondria. This test cannot choose.
scenes.visual: Tube L in both rows is ringed in white. Behind each tube L a dashed white line marks 'starting mix = 1'. A purple glow rises in the teal row's tube L to a mark labelled '9-fold', then, a beat later, in the orange row's tube L to a lower mark labelled '3-fold'; both are clearly above the dashed line, and a small label 'enrichment' sits beside the pair (values from the lesson table: acid phosphatase 45/5, cytochrome oxidase 15/5). On 'plenty of mitochondria', a few small orange compartment cartoons drift visibly inside the orange row's tube L. The bottom bar fills grey and reads 'SAME: both yes' in large letters.
scenes.narration: Test one. Is the protein enriched in tube L, more concentrated than in the starting mix? In the teal twin, yes. In the orange twin, also yes: tube L holds plenty of mitochondria. This test cannot choose.

scenes.tts: Test two reads all five tubes. Each bar is the protein's share in one tube. Two faint tracks show where the lysosome marker and the mitochondrial marker went. If the protein is lysosomal, which track should it trace?
scenes.caption: Test two reads all five tubes. Each bar is the protein's share in one tube. Two faint tracks show where the lysosome marker and the mitochondrial marker went. If the protein is lysosomal, which track should it trace?
scenes.visual: The two tube rows merge into one bar chart of five grey bars, N to S, in the middle of the frame. Two faint dashed tracks are drawn across it and labelled: a TEAL track rising to its tallest point at L, an ORANGE track rising to its tallest at M. Both are computed from the lesson's table, with the small label 'computed from the lesson table' in the corner. Question card at the top: 'Which track should it trace?' The bars pulse gently so nothing is frozen.
scenes.narration: Test two reads all five tubes. Each bar is the protein's share in one tube. Two faint tracks show where the lysosome marker and the mitochondrial marker went. If the protein is lysosomal, which track should it trace?

scenes.visual: Hold the chart with both dashed tracks and the question card on screen. The only motion is the slow pulse of the five grey bars and a soft shimmer running along each dashed track in turn.

scenes.tts: Here the twins disagree. In the lesson's made-up data, the protein follows the lysosome track across all five tubes. A whole profile is stronger evidence than one peak, though still not proof.
scenes.caption: Here the twins disagree. In the lesson's made-up data, the protein follows the lysosome track across all five tubes. A whole profile is stronger evidence than one peak, though still not proof.
scenes.visual: The five grey bars split into a teal set and an orange set that climb onto their own dashed tracks, so the chart shows two clearly different shapes. The bottom bar flips to GOLD and reads 'DIFFERENT'. On 'made-up data', a small corner tag reads 'made-up teaching data', and purple dots drop one by one onto the five points of the TEAL track, sitting close to it but not exactly on it (computed from the lesson table: X 9, 24, 44, 13, 10 against acid phosphatase 8, 25, 45, 12, 10), and a purple line joins them. On 'stronger evidence than one peak', the purple line glows once along its whole length. On 'still not proof', a small white question mark fades in beside the line and stays.
scenes.narration: Here the twins disagree. In the lesson's made-up data, the protein follows the lysosome track across all five tubes. A whole profile is stronger evidence than one peak, though still not proof.

scenes.tts: Tube L leans toward lysosomes, but leaning is not purity. So what is tube L mostly made of? Hold that question.
scenes.caption: Tube L leans toward lysosomes, but leaning is not purity. So what is tube L mostly made of? Hold that question.
scenes.visual: Zoom into tube L alone, drawn large. It fills with cartoon compartments that jostle slowly: teal lysosome shapes, orange mitochondrion shapes and a few grey fragments, mixed with no group drawn as a clear majority. A label beside it reads 'enriched, not pure'; the word 'schematic' sits in the corner. The tube tilts slightly toward the teal group on 'leans', then straightens. On 'mostly made of?', a large white question mark settles over the tube and stays until the cut.
scenes.narration: Tube L leans toward lysosomes, but leaning is not purity. So what is tube L mostly made of? Hold that question.

scenes.tts: Second question: in what order does a protein visit the compartments? Tag one batch and watch. In the teal twin, carriers ferry it between fixed Golgi compartments. In the orange twin, each Golgi compartment itself matures.
scenes.caption: Second question: in what order does a protein visit the compartments? Tag one batch and watch. In the teal twin, carriers ferry it between fixed Golgi compartments. In the orange twin, each Golgi compartment itself matures.
scenes.visual: The tube returns to the two whole twin cells, side by side as at the start. Inside each sit, in a row: an 'ER' block, a Golgi stack of three flat compartments shaded light to dark (cis to trans), and a cluster labelled 'granules'. A short GOLD flash marks one batch of protein in the ER of both cells at the same moment. In BOTH cells a small carrier buds from the ER and fuses with the first Golgi compartment, carrying gold dots, so ER export looks the same on both sides. Teal cell: the three Golgi compartments stay fixed in place and small carriers hop the gold dots from one compartment to the next. Orange cell: the compartment holding the gold dots itself moves along the stack and changes shade from light to dark, while small grey dots (resident enzymes) ride tiny carriers backward. In both cells a granule buds from the last, darkest compartment. Both sides keep moving.
scenes.narration: Second question: in what order does a protein visit the compartments? Tag one batch and watch. In the teal twin, carriers ferry it between fixed Golgi compartments. In the orange twin, each Golgi compartment itself matures.

scenes.tts: In both twins, the gold label lights the E R, then the Golgi, then the granules. The order alone cannot choose. Other tests can.
scenes.caption: In both twins, the gold label lights the E R, then the Golgi, then the granules. The order alone cannot choose. Other tests can.
scenes.visual: In both cells the three regions light GOLD in the order ER, Golgi, granules, with no shared clock and no matching timing between sides; a small label reads 'order only; kinetics not specified'. Under each cell a row of three ticks fills left to right. The bottom bar fills grey and reads 'SAME'. On 'Other tests can', a small gold arrow points off the right edge of the frame.
scenes.narration: In both twins, the gold label lights the E R, then the Golgi, then the granules. The order alone cannot choose. Other tests can.

scenes.tts: Third question: does the protein cause what you see? A drug stops these cancer cells growing. It was built to block one kinase, an enzyme that adds phosphate to proteins. The curve shows growth falling as the dose rises.
scenes.caption: Third question: does the protein cause what you see? A drug stops these cancer cells growing. It was built to block one kinase, an enzyme that adds phosphate to proteins. The curve shows growth falling as the dose rises.
scenes.visual: The compartments fade out and both cells become dividing cells, each accumulating small daughter outlines beside it. Under each cell a computed dose-response curve is drawn on its own axes, falling from left to right, axes labelled 'drug dose' and 'growth'. A small purple block labelled 'the kinase' appears in both cells. A GOLD drug dot docks onto that block in the teal cell; in the orange cell it drifts past the purple block and docks on a second, unlabelled grey block instead.
scenes.narration: Third question: does the protein cause what you see? A drug stops these cancer cells growing. It was built to block one kinase, an enzyme that adds phosphate to proteins. The curve shows growth falling as the dose rises.

scenes.tts: Now take the kinase out of both twins. The cells still grow. Give the drug again. In this two-model cartoon, a drug acting only through that kinase shifts the curve right, to higher doses. One acting only through another target leaves it put. Mixed effects fall between.
scenes.caption: Now take the kinase out of both twins. The cells still grow. Give the drug again. In this two-model cartoon, a drug acting only through that kinase shifts the curve right, to higher doses. One acting only through another target leaves it put. Mixed effects fall between.
scenes.visual: On 'take the kinase out', the purple block vanishes from both cells in a brief white flash and a label 'kinase removed' settles under each. On 'The cells still grow', both cells visibly keep adding daughter outlines. Under the teal cell a predicted TEAL curve slides to the right of its original, toward higher doses, while the original stays as a faint dashed outline. Under the orange cell a predicted ORANGE curve stays exactly on its dashed original. Both predictions are drawn while the narrator names them, and both cells keep dividing slowly.
scenes.narration: Now take the kinase out of both twins. The cells still grow. Give the drug again. In this two-model cartoon, a drug acting only through that kinase shifts the curve right, to higher doses. One acting only through another target leaves it put. Mixed effects fall between.

scenes.tts: The measured curve barely moves. Cells without that kinase are stopped by about the same dose. So in these assays, the drug acts mainly through other targets.
scenes.caption: The measured curve barely moves. Cells without that kinase are stopped by about the same dose. So in these assays, the drug acts mainly through other targets.
scenes.visual: One GOLD measured curve is drawn across both panels, computed, lying on the dashed original in each: it matches the orange prediction and misses the teal one by a wide shaded gap. The bottom bar flips to GOLD and reads 'DIFFERENT', and a tick lands on the orange panel. Small corner label: 'Lin and colleagues, 2017'.
scenes.narration: The measured curve barely moves. Cells without that kinase are stopped by about the same dose. So in these assays, the drug acts mainly through other targets.

scenes.tts: Now silence the protein's message, its m R N A, with R N A interference, and the job fails. But other messages may be silenced too. So put the protein back, in a form the interference cannot touch. How can it be the same protein, yet escape?
scenes.caption: Now silence the protein's message, its m R N A, with R N A interference, and the job fails. But other messages may be silenced too. So put the protein back, in a form the interference cannot touch. How can it be the same protein, yet escape?
scenes.visual: One cell now, centre frame and large, carried over from the teal twin. A purple strand labelled 'm R N A' sits in it making purple protein blobs. A small white hairpin shape pairs with the strand; the strand breaks into fragments, the blobs stop appearing and the cell's division count stalls. On 'other messages may be silenced', a second grey strand nearby also breaks, with a question mark over it. On 'put the protein back', a new purple strand labelled 'resistant copy' drifts in; the hairpin bumps against it and slides off. Purple blobs return and the division count climbs again. On the last question, a white question mark settles beside the resistant strand and stays.
scenes.narration: Now silence the protein's message, its m R N A, with R N A interference, and the job fails. But other messages may be silenced too. So put the protein back, in a form the interference cannot touch. How can it be the same protein, yet escape?

scenes.tts: So: where does it live, in what order does it travel, does it cause the defect? Before any result, ask what each model predicts. Agreeing twins cannot choose.
scenes.caption: So: where does it live, in what order does it travel, does it cause the defect? Before any result, ask what each model predicts. Agreeing twins cannot choose.
scenes.visual: The single cell splits back into the teal and orange twins in their original places. Three small panels fly in across the middle, each a shrunken version of its own scene: the five-bar chart with the purple line on the teal track, the three compartments lighting in order, the two dose-response curves. Each carries its own bottom bar: GOLD 'DIFFERENT', grey 'SAME', GOLD 'DIFFERENT'. On the last sentence the grey 'SAME' panel dims and the two gold panels brighten.
scenes.narration: So: where does it live, in what order does it travel, does it cause the defect? Before any result, ask what each model predicts. Agreeing twins cannot choose.

scenes.line: A result can choose only where the two models disagree.
